raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary (human-written)

`VisionEncoder.Config.conv1` builds the module `conv1_linear`, the one place in the Muse models where a config field and its module differ. Tools that walk the config tree to address parameters by state-dict key (LoRA target selection, adapter name probes in an RL trainer) trip over it: `vision_encoder.conv1.weight` is not a key. The field is renamed to `conv1_linear`; the module, state dict and HF checkpoint mapping are unchanged, so no checkpoint changes.

## Test plan

- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/muse_glimmer`, `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/muse_spark`, `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_build_model_config.py`: 40 passed (renderer/tokenizer test files skipped for missing optional packages on that machine).
- `git grep -P '\bconv1\b'` finds no remaining use of the old field in `torchtitan/models/muse_spark` or the tests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**Claude finished @tianyu-l's task in 1m 30s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41396916658)

**Approve** (please fix the description before merging): [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5732#pullrequestreview)

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging** -- this is a complete, mechanical rename that fixes a real config-FQN/module-FQN mismatch. Module names, the state dict, and the HF mapping are unchanged.

**What this PR does.** It renames `NaViTEncoder.Config.conv1` to `conv1_linear`, so the field has the same name as the module it builds (`self.conv1_linear`). It updates the single flavor builder and the single test that read the field.

**Example.** On `main`, the LoRA transform (`torchtitan/config/transform/lora.py`) matches `target_modules` against the FQNs yielded by `Configurable.traverse`, and those FQNs come from config field names:
```
LoRA(target_modules=["vision_encoder.conv1_linear"])  # documented as a module FQN
  main: traverse yields "vision_encoder.conv1" -> no match, only a logger.warning, encoder patch-embed stays frozen
  PR:   traverse yields "vision_encoder.conv1_linear" -> matches
```

### Must fix
1. PR description: "the one place in the Muse models where a config field and its module differ" is wrong. `block` -> `layers.{i}` in the same encoder still differs (inline comment at `vision_encoder.py:150`). Reword the description so it doesn't promise that exact state-dict-key targeting now works for the whole vision encoder.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Callsites: `git grep -P '\bconv1\b'` finds no remaining references to the old field (flux's unrelated `conv1` aside). Recipes, scripts, and docs have none. `muse_glimmer` reuses `muse_spark_navit_encoder_config`, so the one test update covers it.
- Checkpoints: the native state dict key `vision_encoder.conv1_linear.weight` and the HF mapping (`muse_spark/state_dict_adapter.py:341`, `muse_glimmer/state_dict_adapter.py:114`) were already keyed by the module name, so they are unaffected. No numerics change.
- Follow-up, not in this PR: `torchtitan/models/common/vision_encoder.py:147-148` has the same pattern (`fc1`/`fc2` build `linear_fc1`/`linear_fc2`), so exact LoRA targets on that MLP have the same problem. LoRA also only warns on unmatched targets (`lora.py:302`). Under principle 8, that arguably should raise, since a typo'd target silently trains nothing.
</details>

A maintainer still needs to review.

This same class still has a config field whose name differs from its module: `block` builds `self.layers[str(i)]` (L199-201). `Configurable.traverse` yields `vision_encoder.block.attn.wq`, but the state-dict key is `vision_encoder.layers.0.attn.wq`. The `TODO` at `torchtitan/config/configurable.py:89` points out this exact vision-encoder case. So the description's claim that `conv1` is "the one place in the Muse models where a config field and its module differ" is wrong. A LoRA `target_modules=["vision_encoder.layers.0.attn.wq"]` still matches nothing; suffix targets like `"attn.wq"` do work.

The fix for this PR is to reword the description: the PR fixes the one *renameable* mismatch, and the repeated-block mismatch is a known `traverse` limitation. Changing `block` isn't in scope here, because one config builds N modules, so no rename can make the names agree.
